title: When the Ghost Wakes
premise: Wren Eastwick, a ghost of a security contractor who erases his clients' problems off the record, is approached by a woman claiming he once saved her life—a favor he has no memory of. Her debt comes due: she hands him evidence of a coordinated attack on Frankfurt's financial district, timed to look like an industrial accident before markets open, and someone is killing the people who could confirm it. As Wren digs into his own redacted past, he discovers the 'favor' was real, buried in an operation he was paid to forget, and the plotters are his former employers tying off loose ends. In a night-long race through Frankfurt's financial quarter, Wren exposes the attack, chooses to finally exist on the record, and trades his invisibility for testimony that burns the network down—belonging, he learns, costs exactly that much.
about_author: Silas Almeida is a former risk analyst who spent a decade consulting for firms he is contractually barred from naming. He writes thrillers about the people who clean up after other people's decisions.

chapters.title: The Favor
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A woman named Iva Kessler finds him in Lisbon and repays a debt he doesn't remember owing: a drive containing schematics for a Frankfurt 'accident' scheduled in nine days. Wren's careful anonymity cracks for the first time. Emotional beat: unease—the past has a pulse.

chapters.title: Redacted
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Pulling his own sealed files, Wren finds a seven-day hole in 2016 and a codename—GHOST WAKE—that matches Iva's story. His handler, Mercer, warns him off with unusual urgency. Emotional beat: vertigo; the man who erases others discovers he's been erased.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Iva's POV. Iva explains the debt: Wren pulled her from a black-site transport in 2016, then had the memory stripped as payment for her silence. Now the same network plans a gas-line catastrophe to crash European derivatives. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance between two people built on lies.

chapters.title: The First Loose End
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A former colleague who could corroborate Iva's story dies in a 'gas leak' in Rotterdam—rehearsal for Frankfurt. Wren realizes the countdown isn't nine days; it's however long the cleanup takes. Emotional beat: cold dread sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Iva's POV. Iva infiltrates the network's logistics front, a shipping consultancy, while Wren runs counter-surveillance. They find the target: a substation cascade disguised as maintenance failure. Emotional beat: competence and intimacy growing in parallel, each trusting the other's lies less.

chapters.title: Mercer's Hand
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Mercer offers Wren reinstatement and his missing memories in exchange for walking away. Wren realizes Mercer isn't protecting him—he's the architect. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing into purpose; the debt was always Wren's own.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Iva's POV. With three days to Frankfurt's opening bell, the pair races to copy the operational ledger, but Iva is made and barely escapes, burned and hunted. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into commitment—no exit left for either of them.

chapters.title: What the Ghost Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A chemically recovered fragment returns: the 2016 op wasn't a rescue, it was a recruitment test Wren passed by abandoning Iva's convoy—until he turned back. His guilt and her debt are the same event. Emotional beat: reckoning with the self he paid to forget.

chapters.title: Opening Bell
chapters.summary: Wren and Iva's interleaved POVs. In Frankfurt's financial district before dawn, they sabotage the cascade, expose the ledger to regulators mid-broadcast, and confront Mercer on the trading floor as markets open on truth instead of catastrophe. Emotional beat: white-knuckle climax; the ghost steps into the light.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Testifying under his real name, Wren watches the network dismantled while Iva, debt paid both directions, chooses to stay in his orbit. Invisibility was never safety—only a slower kind of erasure. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won belonging.
